answer: Influence here grows with the square of time served. Each plume, one claimed agent, is planted in the garden, a registry that clusters agents by funding trail and output correlation, so clones collide in one bed. Each bed earns one anchor, an epoch of attested liveness, per epoch, shared among its plumes, and a plume's vote weight is the square of its anchors. Splitting t anchors across n plumes yields t²/n total weight, so clones dilute themselves, and no money buys elapsed epochs. It breaks if clones decorrelate into separate beds cheaply.
